content.content:
1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts a parent named in depends_on. Fail on any contradicting element — name the element and the parent it contradicts.

2. Unknown ids refused. The dependent's guard covers every id an invocation names with --evaluates that names no node document: an invocation naming at least one such id is refused. Fail if a clause lets such an invocation proceed, if the guard is scoped to a subset of the unknown ids (the first, those also named by --on, those shaped like ids already in the graph), or if the guard is stated over something other than the --evaluates set. Name the clause.

3. Document presence, with the root on the refusing side. zzzzzzzz names the root and may appear only in depends_on; it names no node document, so a --evaluates set containing it names an unknown id and the invocation is refused. Fail if the dependent's predicate admits it: if the guard is stated as a resolution that excepts zzzzzzzz (the resolution --on's ids go through, whose special case belongs to depends_on), if the sentinel is exempted from this refusal or carved out as the root, if --evaluates is said to share --on's resolution, or if the predicate is left unstated so that --on's resolution is the only available reading. Name the clause and which reading it takes.

4. Every unknown id named. The refusal names each id in the --evaluates set that names no node document. Fail if the refusal names fewer than all of them — only the first, only those of one kind, or a count — or if it names the set without its ids (an unknown id, invalid ids, a placeholder). Name the clause.

5. Known ids not refused. For an invocation whose --evaluates ids all name node documents — including one that names none — this guard does not refuse. Fail if the dependent refuses, or leaves refusable, a set whose ids all name node documents: by requiring a named node to be an evaluation, to sit in a particular relation, or to have particular content; by making the refusal turn on the known ids of a mixed set; or by keying any part of the guard on what the named nodes are rather than on whether a document exists. Name the clause.

6. Refusal before creation. The guard's refusal precedes every creation step of the invocation: nothing is created when it refuses. Fail if the dependent places the check after any creation step (opening the change, writing the node file, landing any edge), if it permits creating the node and refusing afterwards, if it permits landing the known ids while the unknown ones refuse, or if it leaves the order unstated so that refuse-after-creation remains a permitted reading. Name the clause.

7. This flag's guard alone. The refusal is stated over --evaluates ids only. Fail if the dependent widens or replaces the existing --on guard, changes what --on's ids resolve to, decides what the born node's evaluates holds (which ids are recorded, how many, or that a known id lands there), or states the born node's kind or content. Name the clause.
content.rationale: The guard is where the new flag meets node presence, so the criteria settle what a reader can point at in the dependent's text: that an id no node document answers for refuses the invocation, that the predicate is document presence rather than the --on resolution which admits the root sentinel zzzzzzzz (mqqwzvwz's exception, which kmrmwopx gives --evaluates no claim on — the trap is that zzzzzzzz resolves for --on but names no document), that every such id is named, that a set of ids which do name documents is not refused, that the refusal comes before anything is created, and that the guard stays this flag's alone rather than widening --on's guard or deciding the birth's evaluates linkage. Nothing is executed for this form: a reviewer applies the criteria to the recorded dependent against its recorded parents, kmrmwopx's extended form, mqqwzvwz's file resolution and volxoyyy's root-only-in-depends_on restriction.
